title: API zero-friction onramp — lightweight quickstart and starter-app plan
content:
Goal / north star:
Make the absolute first 15 minutes productive for an engineer who wants to ship a small Redwood-powered feature. Zero cognitive load: minimal config, sensible defaults, helpful errors, and a working app that can be iterated on.

Problem statement (observed):
- New users drop off during 'first code' moment: API keys, environment variables, and model selection create friction.
- Quickstarts are too many choices (which model? streaming vs blocking? embeddings vs chat?) — paralyzes people.
- Local dev experience: mismatch between hosted behavior and local examples (e.g., streaming, chunking) leads to surprise later.

Design principles:
- Minimal: one recommended path that works for 80% of use cases + a short list of opt-ins.
- Reproducible: starter app should run in one command (repo clone + run) with a sandboxed key that gives limited quota.
- Transparent: show token/latency costs inline in examples and why defaults were chosen.
- Expandable: scaffolded extension points (tool wiring, conversation storage) so teams can grow from prototype to production.

Proposed components (MVP):
1) Quickstart CLI command (rdw init) that scaffolds a tiny app for a selected use-case (chat widget, summarizer, search-embed).
   - rdw init --usecase=chat --sdk=js (interactive prompts fallback)
   - Generates: minimal web app, .env.example, Dockerfile (optional), README with where to find tokens + billing/limits link.
2) Play-as-code sample (hosted repo with 3 tiny apps):
   - chat-widget (streaming shows incremental tokens and cost per token)
   - docs-summarizer (upload + embed + rerank sample)
   - template-email-generator (structured tool outputs / function-calls example)
3) Sandbox API key flow for onboarding: temporary dev keys with auto-expiry and generous demo quota, visible in console and copy-pasteable in the quickstart.
4) Local dev container / devcontainer.json that matches hosted runtime (same model selection and streaming behavior).
5) Tiny metrics panel in starter-app for developer: tokens consumed, median latency, suggestion for next-step optimization (batching / smaller context / quantized model).

User stories (quick list):
- As a frontend engineer I want a one-command scaffold that gives me a working chat widget so I can demo LLM features to my PM in <30 minutes.
- As an ML engineer I want the quickstart to include a realistic streaming example and a devcontainer so I can reproduce latency behavior locally.
- As a platform engineer I want the starter app to include clear env var overlays and a way to swap in Dedicated/Private endpoints without code changes.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- rdw init scaffold runs in <60s and app starts with npm/yarn start and shows a working chat response.
- README contains clear steps to get a sandbox key from console and a link to revoke.
- Starter repo passes a smoke test: e2e script that verifies chat flow and a basic embedding+search flow.
- Devcontainer matches hosted runtime: same node/python versions and same default model selection; streaming behavior reproduces in Chrome.
- Developer panel shows token count and a short hint for cost reduction.

Metrics to measure success:
- Time-to-first-response (median time from clone -> first model response) — target < 15 minutes.
- Conversion: % of sandbox users who create a permanent API key within 7 days.
- Drop-off step: where do people stop (console, env, run) — instrument quickstart and console.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Sandbox keys: security vs convenience. Do we allow email-less ephemeral keys? Require SSO to generate?
- Default model choice: one curated for latency/cost (e.g., small chat model) or pick based on detected use-case?
- How opinionated should 'rdw init' be about frontend framework (vanilla JS + fetch vs React)? Keep the default minimal, with optional flags.
- Internationalization: include i18n tips or leave for later?

Implementation sketch / rough timeline:
- Week 0: finalize one recommended path + UX copy for console sandbox key flow.
- Week 1: rdw init prototype + scaffold templates repo (3 apps).
- Week 2: devcontainer and e2e smoke tests + metrics instrumentation.
- Week 3: internal dogfood + docs + small beta in Developer Console.

Risks / mitigation:
- People will fork but not understand quotas -> show clear banner of remaining sandbox quota and an easy upgrade path.
- Starter app mismatches production patterns -> include a tiny section called 'what changes in prod' that lists config toggles.

Parking lot / nice-to-have (post-MVP):
- Playground-as-code: embed sandbox in console so users can click "create sandbox app" and see a live deploy.
- One-click deploy to Vercel / Cloud Run with automatic secrets injection for paid customers (only after key is verified).
- Multi-lang SDK examples auto-generated from OpenAPI / snippets.
- Starter templates for common verticals (support assistant, code assistant, product copywriter).

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Align with Console PM (Ravi) on sandbox key policy and quotas. (Ravi to confirm by Thu)
- Spike rdw init minimal CLI and choose default front-end target (vanilla + tiny CSS).
- Create starter repo skeleton and add to quickstarts org; add smoke test skeleton.

Notes / random thoughts:
- Could show a tiny 'cost preview' during typing: estimate token cost for the last message based on model.
- Include an 'explain defaults' modal: why we chose model X, why streaming on by default for chat.
- Keep copy short: onboarding text should be skimmable and actionable.

References / links:
- quickstarts issues (see linked artifacts)
- earlier "first-run warmup" notes in drive (search: first-run warmup flow)

End of jot — rough, messy, intentionally. Will iterate after sync with Console and SDK leads.
